SITE DECISIONS - all 10 CRITICAL sites explicitly recorded:
  S1 (640,347), S4 (371,351), S5 (521,350) -> JUNCTION. Three clean tees on the top rail where the column drops to a zener/diode. No hop, no jog, rail continuous. Reading any of them as a crossing would leave that column's upper device with a dangling terminal, which is electrically impossible.
  S23 (384,638), S25 (656,638) -> JUNCTION. Clean tees on the bottom rail where the column lead lands on it. Same argument: a crossing would strand the lower device of that column.
  S8 (535,484), S9 (650,484), S10 (374,486) -> JUNCTION. All three are four-way crossings of the middle rail with a column, and all three carry an unmistakable SOLDER DOT. Verified at the pixel level with inkmap: at S10 the ink swells to 11 px across over rows 481-489 against a 3 px stroke, at S8 to 10 px over rows 477-488, at S9 to 14 px over rows 479-485. Those are symmetric blobs ~3-4x the stroke width in both axes, i.e. real dots, not stroke overlap.
  S12 (794,489) deg4 -> JUNCTION (JUDGEMENT CALL). This is the middle rail crossing the right-hand frame column, which carries diode #6 above and diode #14 below. Plain X: no solder dot (inkmap at (787,490) shows the ink widening only to 6 px over 4 rows, which is exactly what two ~3-4 px strokes crossing produce - compare the 11-14 px blobs at S8/S9/S10) and no hop or jog. I read it as a junction for three reasons. (a) Ink prior for this dataset: the drafter signals 'not connected' with a hop or a sideways jog, and there is not a single hop anywhere on this sheet. (b) The structure is a regular 3-rail ladder in which every one of the five columns has exactly one device between top and middle and one between middle and bottom; that layout is only meaningful if the middle rail taps every column. (c) Decisive: S13 (below) is also an undotted four-way crossing and it must be a junction, so 'undotted' does not mean 'crossing' on this sheet - the drafter simply dotted the three interior crossings and not the two frame-edge ones. THE OTHER READING would have split n5 into {diode 6.1, diode 14.1} (the floating midpoint of two series diodes) and {4uH 8.1, R2k 10.0}; both halves are electrically sane, which is why this is a judgement call rather than a forced answer, but it would make the right-hand column a pointless series diode pair and leave the 2k load fed only through the 4uH.
  S13 (123,494) deg4 -> JUNCTION (JUDGEMENT CALL, but strongly constrained). The middle rail crossing the left-hand source column. Again a plain undotted X with no hop. Read as a junction, the V-AC bottom terminal and the I-DC top terminal both sit on the GND net, i.e. an AC source referenced to ground and a current source injecting into the bottom rail from ground - the standard, and clearly intended, arrangement; that is also why the drafter carried the middle rail past the column to the left to hang the GND symbol #9 off it. THE OTHER READING would put {V-AC 2.1, I-DC 11.0} on their own two-terminal floating net and would leave the AC source in series with the ideal current source, a degenerate branch in which the voltage source can have no effect, while the GND-bearing middle rail would connect to nothing but col A and the 9uF cap. I took the junction reading and note that the dot habit alone would have argued the other way.
  Non-critical sites, all left at the tracer default and none of them wire-to-wire: S6 (146,403) and S22 (168,565) are the '8K'/'1kHz' and '3A' labels touching the source symbols; S15 (437,515) and S18 (470,519) are the '9uF' label; S16 (736,514) and S17 (744,515) are the '4uH' label; S24 (533,638) is the tee where the col B zener lands on the bottom rail next to the 1uH inductor - a genuine tee, already inside n7/n8 and not netlist-changing.

PORT FIXES:

Repointed: t0 -> p1@(529,588) (bottom lead to the bottom rail, unchanged) and t1 -> p0@(530,538) (top lead up to the middle rail at col B). Terminal order is not scored for a 2-terminal zener.
  #7 Capacitor (9uF): the tracer resolved only 1 of 2 terminals. Its left lead is real - the middle rail runs in from col A and the traced edge e26 ends at (424,487), 7 px short of the component box at x=431, which is why the port finder missed it. Since there is no port index to point terminal 0 at, I pinned it directly with manual_nets: 7.0 = '0'. Justification: edge e26 runs (424,487)->(378,486) and touches site S10, the dotted col-A junction, so it is unambiguously part of the middle-rail left segment, i.e. net 0. Confirmed at the pixel level: the horizontal rail ink is continuous from x<400 to x=448 and abuts the cap's left plate at x=440-443, with the plate gap and the right plate at x=453-459 beyond it.
  All other ports confirmed correct in the _comps montages, including the two source polarities (V-AC top/bottom, I-DC top/bottom) and both GND stems. The 'unused port' candidates on #8 (4uH) and #11 (I-DC) are the 'uH' and '3A' label ink touching the boxes, not leads.

CLASSES: all 19 match the drawing. The three zeners (#3, #4, #13) and the fourth (#4 col C) show the bent/S-terminated cathode bar and are labelled '5V'; the five plain diodes (#5, #6, #12, #14, #15) have a straight cathode bar. #9 at (39,504) is a GND symbol drawn rotated 90 degrees (bars vertical, decreasing in length to the left) - easy to mistake for stray ink or a '1' but it is unmistakably a ground, and its presence is what fixes the middle-rail left segment as net 0. No re-classification needed.
